# xcfs

> xcfs gives parallel AI coding agents their own git worktrees of one Xcode (iOS or macOS) project without a cold
> build per worktree: a pool of checkouts kept built at the baseline, an incremental build session instead of
> xcodebuild's fixed cost, a one-file compile check, one simulator per checkout, and cleanup that removes everything a
> checkout made (DerivedData included) and nothing that holds unsaved work. It installs as Claude Code
> WorktreeCreate / WorktreeRemove / SessionEnd hooks (`xcfs hook install --apply`), and every command answers in JSON
> for other agent tools. macOS on APFS, Xcode, Python 3.9+ standard library; MIT; `brew install PatrickSCLin/xcfs/xcfs`.

Measured with three agents at once on public apps: later batches 1.3–2.2× faster on two apps (1.8–2.7× with the opt-in experimental Swift driver) than plain `git worktree` +
`xcodebuild` (the first batch on a fresh pool is slower, it pays for the warm-up), less peak memory (8–12 against 24–25 GB on Ice Cubes, 11–13 against 15–16 GB on Wikipedia), and
nothing left in DerivedData (plain worktrees left 1.5–2.9 GB each).

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/PatrickSCLin/xcfs/blob/main/README.md): what it solves, benchmarks, commands, configuration
- [Using xcfs from an AI agent](https://github.com/PatrickSCLin/xcfs/blob/main/docs/agents.md): the commands, the hooks, exit codes and what to do on each
- [What is stable](https://github.com/PatrickSCLin/xcfs/blob/main/docs/stability.md): JSON fields, exit codes and config keys scripts can rely on
- [Benchmarks](https://github.com/PatrickSCLin/xcfs/blob/main/docs/benchmark.md): method, tables, caveats; raw results in bench/results
- [Xcode versions](https://github.com/PatrickSCLin/xcfs/blob/main/docs/xcode-versions.md): what was run on which Xcode, and what happens on others

## Optional

- [Why not just git worktree](https://github.com/PatrickSCLin/xcfs/blob/main/docs/why-not-plain-worktrees.md): plain worktrees, a shared DerivedData, long-lived worktrees, measured
- [Design](https://github.com/PatrickSCLin/xcfs/blob/main/docs/design.md): architecture, adapter interface, slot lifecycle, edge cases, what is not verified
- [Build systems](https://github.com/PatrickSCLin/xcfs/blob/main/docs/build-systems.md): Bazel, Buck2, Tuist, compiler caches, and what each is worth here
- [The experimental Swift driver](https://github.com/PatrickSCLin/xcfs/blob/main/docs/incremental-swift.md): the patch and what upstream would need
